title: Heat Pump Rebates in Windsor 2026: Older Homes and Up to $7,500
desc: Windsor heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: 68% of homes predate 1981, and the rate depends on whether you heat with gas, electric, oil or propane.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Windsor has 94,275 households, and 68% live in homes built before 1981. January averages -6.2°C, milder than most of Ontario, which widens the choice of models and sizing.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Windsor
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 34,370 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981 in Windsor, 72% of households in an eligible type and 63% owning. 7.2% report needing major repairs, one of the higher rates in our data. A house needing repairs may be a good moment to plan the ductwork and electrical service for a heat pump.

A heat pump needs electrical capacity, and an older house may have a small panel. The program requires installation to meet code and permitting. Ask the contractor whether a panel upgrade is needed, and what it costs, because it is not part of the rebate. Photos of the existing electrical or heating equipment go with the pre-approval.

With a January low of -6.2°C and a record of -28.0°C, a cold-climate model covers most of the winter. Gas and propane homes can choose sizing options A to D, and oil, wood and electric homes C or D. The program's cold-climate rules still apply to every model.

A rented heat pump is eligible for any primary heating fuel at $500 per ton up to $2,000 for air-source or $3,000 flat for ground-source. The signed rental agreement replaces the invoice at the post-installation step.

The pre-installation application needs photos of the existing heating equipment and its nameplate. A Windsor home with an old furnace should have the nameplate legible before the contractor visits, and an electrically heated home needs baseboard photos from at least three areas. Missing photos delay approval, and the work cannot start until approval is in writing.

The contractor has 30 days to file the post-installation application with the final itemized invoice, photographs of the installed equipment and the thermostat, and installation details. Windsor owners should ask for the filing date, and the cheque follows within 60 days of approval.
claim_steps: Check whether your electrical panel can take a heat pump.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
